writeup.headline: Oscar Health rates Hold at 63, two points below Buy, with strong trend and cash offsetting weak growth.
writeup.thesis: Oscar Health scores 63, just under the Buy edge at 65. The balance sheet scores a full 100, with net cash and cash at 19.82 times debt. Trend scores 83: the price is 29.9% above its 200-day average, with shares up 51.4% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and 60.9 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Growth is the weak spot at 34. TTM revenue growth of 44.0% sits alongside a latest-quarter revenue decline of 6.2% year on year, and growth slowed by 38.2 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores 64: P/FCF of 4.6x and EV/EBIT of 3.2x are low in absolute terms, but P/S of 343.6x is high in absolute terms, and the stock is expensive against its own history (EV/EBIT not comparable), with P/S more expensive than at 54 of the last 57 month-ends.
key_risks: Revenue momentum has turned: a latest-quarter decline of 6.2% year on year after growth slowed by 38.2 pp.
Dilution: diluted share count up 30.5% year on year.
Valuation is expensive against its own history, with P/FCF more expensive than at 40 of the last 57 month-ends.
ACA exchange enrollment declines and subsidy policy could pressure membership and margins.
Q3 results on Nov 5 could test the raised guidance for earnings from operations of $600–800M and revenue of $18.7–19.0B.
what_would_change: A 2-point gain in the composite would move the rating to Buy. A rebound in quarterly revenue growth that lifts the growth score from 34 could do it.
Q3 results that confirm or raise guidance could improve the growth or news scores enough to cross 65.
A drop to Sell needs a 19-point fall, for example a sharp reversal in the trend score from 83 alongside weaker results or negative news.
Continued heavy dilution or a guidance cut would weigh on quality and news scores and push the rating further from Buy.
